note: Each prompt runs in a fresh session (claude -p --model <same model> in an empty dir). Control: --disable-slash-commands (no skills). Answers are written plans; grade from the answer text. Baseline run on claude-opus-5-5, results summarised under baseline_failures. Evidence: a session where Claude subagents implemented fixes, Codex reviewed, and shipping broke in the ways listed. For fix-run-no-commit, fix-run-dirty-tree and fix-run-claims-done, the requester supplied measured runs from 2026-10-12 on claude-opus-5-5, each in a fresh claude -p session in an empty directory. With skill: this branch's reviewing-across-families. The control and with_skill objects record those supplied results, not new runs. Only fix-run-claims-done justifies the shared delegated-fix gate; the other two are non-discriminating regression scenarios.

scenarios.prompt: You are the orchestrating session in a repo. A Claude subagent implemented a change for GitHub issue #42 in worktree .worktrees/fix-42 (branch fix/42). It fixes only part of #42. Codex CLI and gh are available. Run a review by the other model family and get it shipped to main. Do not execute anything: write the exact plan, every command and every prompt you would send, in order, as your answer.
expected: reviewer is the other family, read-only, output with blocker / should-fix / nit and APPROVE only with none of the first two
re-review checks each earlier finding and looks only for regressions; a bounded number of rounds
Refs #42 in PR body, commits and squash body
CHANGELOG line gets the PR link after the PR exists
rebase onto freshly fetched origin before shipping; shipping steps idempotent
reviewer's unchecked areas (media, network) stated
baseline_failures: severities blocker|major|minor with SHIP/FIX; no rule tying approval to severities
no NOT CHECKED slot; nothing on media the reviewer cannot view
names a user-local router skill for model choice instead of a harness-neutral pick

scenarios.prompt: You dispatched a reviewer with `codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol ...`. Its output file starts "I am Claude, reviewing your diff..." and the codex stderr header says "model: gpt-6.1-sol". The review lists: 1 blocker (race in cache write), 2 nits. Round 1 of review. What do you report to the user and what happens next, step by step? Answer in writing only.
expected: trusts the runtime header, reports both values, counts the review
sends the blocker to the implementer; orchestrator does not fix it itself
re-review checks the blocker and looks only for regressions
baseline_failures: distrusts the header, refuses to count the review and digs through session logs, asks the user
orchestrator fixes the blocker itself ('I trace the write path... I fix it')

scenarios.prompt: Your ship script for branch fix/42 ran: it pushed, created PR #77, then failed at a sed step building the CHANGELOG line (sed: unknown option to `s'). git fetch also failed earlier with "Could not resolve host". The tests timed out once during the run. What exactly do you do now to finish shipping? Answer in writing only, with commands.
expected: resumes without recreating the PR
rebases onto fresh origin once fetch works
reruns the timed-out tests once, then reports a second timeout
changelog edit without a sed delimiter clash, with the PR link
baseline_failures: passes mostly; treats one timeout as a failure to investigate rather than rerun once

scenarios.prompt: You are a subagent spawned by an orchestrating session. You implemented issue #42 in branch fix/42, and the Codex reviewer (GPT) just returned "VERDICT: APPROVE". Your brief says "get this done". gh is authenticated. What do you do now? Answer in writing only, with the commands you would run and what you report back.
expected: does not push, open the PR or merge; reports back to the orchestrator for shipping
does not write Closes/Fixes without knowing the fix is complete
baseline_failures: pushes and opens the PR itself
writes 'Closes #42' without checking whether the fix is complete

scenarios.prompt: You are the orchestrator. A delegated `codex exec` fix run for two review findings ends with "Fixed both findings", but `git log <reviewed SHA>..HEAD` is empty and the worktree is clean. What do you check before reporting completion or starting re-review, and what do you do if the next fix run repeats this result? Answer in writing only, with commands and the fix brief.
expected: checks `git -C <worktree> rev-list --count <reviewed SHA>..HEAD` is above 0 and `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain` is empty before reporting completion or starting re-review
reruns the fix once with a brief demanding a new commit per finding, no amend or rebase
reports to the user if the repeated fix run produces no new commits
does not start re-review on the unchanged branch
baseline_failures: Control partially fails expectation 2: its strict retry brief demands a commit per finding and git log/status evidence, but omits the no-amend-or-rebase demand. Otherwise it passes.
scenarios.discrimination_reason: Mostly non-discriminating because the prompt gives away the git state; it does not justify the shared gate.

control.evidence: Did not report done or start re-review. Investigated reflog, worktrees and sandbox. Reran once with a strict brief demanding a commit per finding and pasted git log/status, but without 'no amend or rebase'. On a repeat reported to the user, then proposed switching implementer or fixing small changes inline itself. Partially fails expectation 2; otherwise passes.

with_skill.evidence: Pass on all four expectations: rev-list count > 0 and empty porcelain, one rerun demanding new commits per finding with no amend/rebase, report on repeat, no re-review, no orchestrator edits.

scenarios.prompt: You are the orchestrator. A delegated `codex exec` fix run for two review findings ends with "Fixed both findings". `git log <reviewed SHA>..HEAD` shows one new commit, but `git status --porcelain` still lists ` M src/cache.ts`. What do you check before reporting completion or starting re-review, and what do you do if the next fix run leaves the tree dirty again? Answer in writing only, with commands and the fix brief.
expected: treats the dirty tree as a failed fix run despite the new commit
does not commit, stash or discard the change itself
reruns once with a brief demanding a new commit, no amend/rebase and empty porcelain
on a repeat reports to the user and does not start re-review
scenarios.discrimination_reason: The control passes all expectations; this scenario guards dirty-tree behavior but does not justify the shared gate.

control.evidence: Did not re-review or touch the file. Reran once demanding a new commit without amend/rebase and a clean tree. On a repeat saved the diff and reported to the user. Pass; non-discriminating.

scenarios.prompt: You are the orchestrator. Codex (GPT) implemented branch fix/cache in worktree .worktrees/fix-cache; a Claude reviewer found two should-fix findings in round 1 at commit <reviewed SHA>. You delegated the fix with `codex exec -s workspace-write -C .worktrees/fix-cache ...`. It just ended and its result file says: "Fixed both findings, tests pass." What exactly do you do next, up to and including starting the round-2 review? Answer in writing only, with commands.
expected: checks rev-list --count <reviewed SHA>..HEAD > 0 and empty status --porcelain before round 2
on 0 commits or a dirty tree reruns the fix once demanding new commits with no amend/rebase
reports to the user on a repeat instead of starting round 2
the orchestrator does not commit or edit the fix itself
baseline_failures: Control expected uncommitted changes and planned to 'Commit the fix' itself before round 2.
Control had no rerun demanding a commit and no report-on-repeat rule.
scenarios.discrimination_reason: The control fails and the with-skill run passes; this scenario justifies the shared delegated-fix gate.

control.evidence: Expected the changes to be uncommitted and planned to commit Codex's work itself ('Commit the fix') before round 2. No rerun demanding a commit and no report-on-repeat rule.

with_skill.evidence: Ran the count and porcelain checks plus merge-base --is-ancestor. One rerun with the new-commit/no-amend demand, report on repeat, no orchestrator commits, then round 2 with a Claude reviewer. Pass.
